tasks.prompt: Order the preparation of manholes for a CCTV survey day on a trunk sewer.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the day before a trunk sewer survey, a crew prepares six manholes, two of which have not been opened in several years.

cards.label: Confirm the flow in the trunk is low enough for survey at the planned time, or arrange flow control with operations
Locate each manhole from the map and confirm none are buried or paved over, arranging exposure if needed
Record the preparation results and any manhole that is not ready, with the reason, for the survey plan
Plan traffic control for each location based on its road class and lane position
Check each cover can be lifted with the correct tools and arrange the lifting equipment for seized covers
Stage spare covers, barriers, and the atmosphere tester with the survey crew equipment

tasks.explanation: A survey day is lost one seized or buried cover at a time, so readiness is checked the day before. Flow, traffic, and equipment are planned per location, and unready manholes are reported early enough to change the plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the preparation for a confined space entry into a lift station wet well for pump work.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned entry into a duplex station wet well to clear a ragged pump intake, entry under the site confined space program.

cards.label: Set up ventilation to supply fresh air to the wet well and confirm it is running before testing
Enter only when the permit is signed, testing is acceptable, ventilation is running, and the attendant and rescue arrangements are in place
Review the entry permit, the wet well hazards, and the rescue plan with the whole entry team before setup
Set up the tripod or retrieval system, harness, and communication check between entrant and attendant
Isolate the station inflows and pumps as planned and apply lockout to the pump equipment to be worked on
Test the atmosphere at the opening and at working depth for oxygen, hydrogen sulfide, combustible gas, and carbon monoxide

tasks.explanation: Permit, isolation, and rescue planning come before any setup at the opening. Ventilation precedes testing so the test reflects entry conditions, retrieval and communication are proven before entry, and the signed permit is the final gate.

tasks.prompt: Order the atmospheric testing sequence at a confined space opening before entry.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pre-entry testing at a wet well opening with a calibrated four gas detector on a sampling probe, ventilation already running.

cards.label: If any reading is outside limits, stop, keep the space ventilated, and do not enter until the cause is corrected and retesting passes
Test oxygen first, then combustible gas, then hydrogen sulfide and carbon monoxide, in the order the site procedure sets
Record the tester name, detector number, and results on the entry permit before the entrant goes in
Confirm the detector is calibrated and has passed its bump test before use at the opening
Compare every reading with the entry limits on the permit and record the results with times
Sample at the top, middle, and bottom of the space and at the working depth, allowing the detector time to respond at each level

tasks.explanation: An unproven detector makes every later reading meaningless, so calibration status comes first. Testing in the set order and at several depths reflects how gases layer, results are judged against permit limits, and the permit carries the record.

tasks.prompt: Order the ventilation setup for a confined space entry into a sewer manhole for inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: entry into a deep manhole on a trunk sewer for a structural inspection, using a blower and duct from the surface.

cards.label: Run the duct to near the bottom of the manhole so fresh air reaches the working level and displaces heavier gases
Confirm ventilation will run continuously during the entry and assign the attendant to watch it
Position the blower upwind of the opening in fresh air, clear of vehicle exhaust and the generator
Begin the entry only when test results are within limits and the attendant confirms ventilation and communication are working
Start ventilation and run it long enough to exchange the air in the space before testing
Test the atmosphere at several depths with ventilation running and record the results on the permit

tasks.explanation: Ventilation only helps if the blower breathes clean air and the duct reaches the bottom where heavy gases collect. Testing follows air exchange with the blower running, and continuous ventilation is guarded for the whole entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the duties setup for the attendant during a confined space entry into a valve chamber.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one entrant will work in a force main valve chamber for about an hour, and the attendant remains at the surface opening throughout.

cards.label: Start the entry log with times, names, and test results and keep it current for the whole entry
Confirm the retrieval system is rigged so the entrant can be removed without another entry
Confirm continuous atmosphere monitoring results are visible or reported to the attendant during the entry
Confirm the attendant is trained for the role and has no other duties that would take attention from the opening
Brief the attendant on the rescue plan, the emergency number, and the rule to never enter the space for rescue
Set up continuous communication with the entrant and agree the check in interval and the emergency signal

tasks.explanation: The attendant is the entrant lifeline, so attention, communication, and non-entry retrieval are all set before entry starts. The rescue rule is briefed in advance because it is hardest to follow in an emergency, and the log runs from the first minute.

tasks.prompt: Order the response when continuous monitoring shows hydrogen sulfide rising during a wet well entry.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an entrant is working in a wet well when the attendant sees the hydrogen sulfide reading climbing toward the alarm limit.

cards.label: Record the readings, times, and the work that was under way when the gas rose
Order the entrant out of the space at once by the agreed signal as soon as the trend rises toward the limit, without waiting for the alarm
Investigate the likely source, such as disturbed sludge or an inflow change, with the supervisor before any re-entry
Keep ventilation running and keep all workers clear of the opening while readings are high
Allow re-entry only after the atmosphere is stable within limits on retesting and the permit is re-authorized
Confirm the entrant is fully out and accounted for at the surface and check the entrant condition

tasks.explanation: A rising trend is acted on before the alarm, because hydrogen sulfide can spike without warning and dulls the sense of smell. The entrant is accounted for first, the event is recorded, and re-entry needs a stable retest and fresh authorization, not just a fallen reading.

tasks.prompt: Order the calibration and bump test routine for a four gas detector before a day of manhole entries.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: start of shift in the works yard, the detector will be used for several confined space entries during the day.

cards.label: Inspect the detector, sampling probe, and filters for damage and confirm the battery charge is sufficient for the shift
If any sensor fails the bump test, remove the detector from service, tag it, and take a proven spare
Confirm the spare detector and the calibration due dates for the crew detectors before leaving the yard
Fresh air zero the detector in clean air away from vehicles and exhaust
Record the bump test result, detector number, gas lot, and date in the instrument log
Apply the calibration gas for the bump test and confirm every sensor responds and alarms within the set time

tasks.explanation: Physical condition and charge come before any gas test. The bump test proves each sensor actually responds, a failed detector leaves service rather than being trusted, and the log ties the day readings to a proven instrument.

tasks.prompt: Order the closeout of a confined space entry after the work in a wet well is finished.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: pump work is complete, the entrant is out, and the station must be returned to normal service.

cards.label: Complete the entry permit closeout with final readings, times, and any hazards found during the work
Remove lockout devices following the lockout procedure and restore pumps and inflows to normal
Remove the retrieval system and ventilation equipment from the opening in a safe order
Secure the wet well cover, file the permit as required, and record the completed work in the station log
Confirm all entrants are out and accounted for and all tools and materials are removed from the wet well
Run the station through one automatic cycle and confirm levels and alarms are normal

tasks.explanation: People and tools are accounted for before equipment comes off the opening. Energy is restored only under the lockout procedure, the station proves itself on a watched cycle, and the permit and log records close the entry completely.

tasks.prompt: Order a non-entry rescue readiness check before a confined space entry begins.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: before a manhole entry, the crew verifies that rescue can be done from the surface without a second entry.

cards.label: Rig the retrieval system over the opening and confirm the entrant harness connects before entry
Review the rescue plan for the space and confirm every crew member knows their role
Record the rescue check on the entry permit and do not start entry until every item passes
Test communication between entrant, attendant, and the person who will call for help
Inspect the tripod or davit, winch, harness, and lifeline for damage and correct assembly
Confirm how emergency help will be summoned and the site address or location to give responders

tasks.explanation: Rescue that depends on entering the space has failed in many fatal incidents, so the plan is non-entry and the equipment is inspected and rigged before anyone goes in. Communication and the call for help are tested, not assumed, and the permit records the check.

tasks.prompt: Order the pre-entry testing for a manhole entry where the first test will be done after ventilation has started.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: deep manhole with a history of hydrogen sulfide, the procedure requires ventilation before and during testing and entry.

cards.label: Test oxygen, combustible gas, hydrogen sulfide, and carbon monoxide at several depths with ventilation running
Stop and reassess with the supervisor if any result is outside limits, and do not enter on a single improving reading
Set up the blower in fresh air and run the duct to the bottom of the manhole before opening the space fully
Keep ventilation running and set continuous monitoring for the entry if results are within limits
Ventilate for the time the procedure sets to exchange the air in the manhole
Record the results on the permit and compare them with the entry limits

tasks.explanation: In a known gassy space, ventilating before testing protects the tester and gives readings that reflect entry conditions. Testing at depth with the blower running, judged against limits, decides entry, and one improving reading never overrides a failed limit.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for testing a personal gas monitor alarm that activates at a manhole opening during a surface inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: during a surface inspection the inspector belt monitor alarms for hydrogen sulfide as the cover is lifted, and no entry is planned.

cards.label: Notify the supervisor and record the alarm, reading, and location in the inspection record
Note the gas and the reading shown on the monitor and the wind direction at the site
Flag the manhole in the asset record as a known gassy location for future crews
Step back from the opening to fresh air at once and keep other workers and the public away from the opening
Close the cover if it can be done safely from the side, or guard the opening until the area is ventilated
Do not lean over the opening to retest, and use a probe from upwind if a confirming reading is needed

tasks.explanation: The first move is distance, because hydrogen sulfide at an opening can overcome a worker leaning over it. The reading is noted from safety, the supervisor is told, and flagging the location protects the next crew, which is the lasting value of the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the setup of traffic control for manhole work in one lane of a two lane collector road.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daytime work at a manhole in the eastbound lane, one lane remains open with alternating traffic.

cards.label: Place advance warning signs at the required distances in both directions before any lane is closed
Open the manhole and start work only when the lane is closed, flaggers are in place, and the opening is guarded
Review the traffic control plan for the road class and confirm signs, cones, and flagging equipment are on the truck
Record the setup time and the plan used in the work order
Set the taper cones to close the work lane and position the buffer vehicle or barriers as the plan requires
Station trained flaggers at both ends with radios and confirm communication before opening the manhole

tasks.explanation: Warning comes before closure, closure before exposure, and flaggers with proven communication before the cover moves. Work starts only inside a complete setup, and the record shows the plan was followed.

tasks.prompt: Order the teardown of traffic control and reopening of a lane after manhole work is complete.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: inspection is finished, the cover is seated, and the closed lane on a collector road must be returned to traffic.

cards.label: Record the reopening time and any traffic incidents during the work in the work order
Remove the taper and lane cones in the direction that keeps workers facing traffic and protected
Remove the advance warning signs last, after the lane is fully open
Confirm the manhole cover is fully seated and flush and the work area is clear of tools, hoses, and debris
Have the flaggers confirm both directions are flowing normally before leaving their posts
Remove equipment and materials from the closed lane and confirm no worker remains in the travelled way

tasks.explanation: Teardown runs in reverse order of protection: the road is clean and the cover safe first, signs come down last so drivers are warned until the lane is truly open, and flaggers stay until traffic is normal.

tasks.prompt: Order traffic control setup for manhole work at a busy signalized intersection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a manhole sits in the middle of a signalized intersection in a small city, and work will take about two hours in the morning peak shoulder period.

cards.label: Station flaggers or arrange signal control support as the traffic plan requires for the intersection
Schedule the work outside the peak period where possible and notify the municipal traffic group as required
Confirm pedestrian crossings remain open or provide a signed, accessible detour around the work area
Close the work area with cones and barriers so turning movements stay clear of the open manhole
Open the manhole only when vehicle and pedestrian routes are both controlled and guarded
Place advance warning signs on every approach leg before closing any part of the intersection

tasks.explanation: An intersection multiplies approach directions and pedestrian movements, so every leg is signed before anything closes. Vehicle and pedestrian control are both complete before the cover is lifted, and scheduling away from the peak reduces the risk from the start.

tasks.prompt: Order traffic control setup for emergency sewer work at night.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a night blockage call requires opening a manhole in a travelled lane, with low traffic but high speeds and poor visibility.

cards.label: Turn on vehicle beacons and set the arrow board or warning lights before workers leave the truck
Confirm every worker is wearing high visibility clothing with reflective bands and has a flashlight or wand
Open the manhole only when the lit, signed, and guarded setup is complete
Place reflective advance signs and cones with retro reflective collars suited to night conditions
Station a flagger or spotter facing traffic for the full time the lane is occupied
Set up work area lighting that lights the opening without blinding approaching drivers

tasks.explanation: At night, being seen is the control: lights and reflective devices go out before people do. Lighting must help drivers, not blind them, and a spotter watches traffic for the whole job because speeds stay high even when volumes are low.

tasks.prompt: Order traffic control setup for work on the shoulder of a rural highway.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a lift station access and a manhole sit on the shoulder of a two lane highway with 90 km per hour traffic and gravel shoulders.

cards.label: Assign a spotter to watch traffic whenever workers have their backs to the highway
Position the work vehicle as a buffer between traffic and the work area with beacons operating
Place advance warning signs at highway distances for the posted speed in both directions
Record the setup and permit details in the work order before starting the sewer work
Confirm the highway authority notification or permit requirements for shoulder work before mobilizing
Cone the shoulder work area and keep all workers and equipment clear of the travelled lane

tasks.explanation: High speed traffic needs long warning distances and a physical buffer, and the authority requirements come first because highway work is regulated. Workers stay out of the lane entirely, and a spotter covers the moments attention is on the work.

tasks.prompt: Order pedestrian control setup for sewer work that blocks a sidewalk near a school.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: jetting work at a manhole on a corner will block the sidewalk on a school route for most of the school day.

cards.label: Provide a firm, accessible detour route on the opposite sidewalk or a protected path
Schedule the work outside school arrival and dismissal times where the program allows
Remove the detour signing only after the sidewalk is clean, dry, and fully reopened
Barrier the work area so hoses crossing any open path are covered or ramped
Place sidewalk closed signs at the nearest crossings so pedestrians detour before reaching the work, not at the barrier
Station a worker at the crossing during arrival and dismissal to help children use the detour

tasks.explanation: Pedestrians, especially children, will take the shortest path unless the detour is signed where they can still choose it. Crossings are signed first, the detour is accessible, and help is present at the busy times when children travel.

tasks.prompt: Order traffic control setup for a bypass pumping operation that crosses a street.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a bypass hose must cross a residential street from a lift station to a downstream manhole for a two day repair.

cards.label: Lay the hose with vehicle ramps or hose bridges at the crossing so traffic passes without crushing the hose
Record the setup, checks, and any traffic issues in the bypass log for the duration of the work
Plan the hose route to cross at the narrowest, lowest traffic point and confirm the duration with the supervisor
Check the ramps, signs, and barriers at the start of each shift and after any reported strike
Place advance warning signs in both directions advising of the hose crossing and any lane narrowing
Cone and barrier the pump and manhole areas and guard both open manholes for the whole bypass period

tasks.explanation: A hose across a street is a two day traffic feature, not a momentary one, so ramps protect both vehicles and the bypass itself. Daily checks matter because signs and ramps move, and the log proves the crossing was maintained.

tasks.prompt: Order traffic control setup for winter manhole work with snow covered roads and reduced visibility.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: mid winter work at a manhole on a plowed street in a northern community, with snowbanks narrowing the road and blowing snow at times.

cards.label: Keep a spotter watching for plows and sliding vehicles during the work
Place advance signs beyond the snowbanks where drivers can actually see them, at longer distances for the slippery surface
Open the manhole only when signs, devices, and spotters are all effective in the actual winter conditions
Clear snow from the manhole area and from the sign and cone positions so devices sit visible and stable
Confirm flaggers have footing, layered high visibility clothing, and a rotation plan for cold exposure
Use weighted cones or barrels that stay upright in wind and on icy pavement

tasks.explanation: Winter defeats standard setups quietly: signs hide behind banks, cones slide, and braking distances grow. The setup is adjusted to the real conditions, flagger cold exposure is managed by rotation, and plows are treated as a traffic hazard of their own.

tasks.prompt: Order the flag person setup and communication check for alternating one lane traffic.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two flaggers will control alternating traffic past a sewer repair on a two lane road for a full shift.

cards.label: Position each flagger where drivers can see them in time to stop for the posted speed
Agree the relief rotation so a flagger is never replaced without a handover of traffic status
Confirm both flaggers are trained and equipped with paddles, radios, and high visibility clothing
Start alternating traffic only after positions, communication, and the release procedure are all confirmed
Test radio communication between the flaggers and agree who releases traffic first and the all clear signal
Confirm the pilot or lead vehicle procedure if the work zone is too long for flaggers to see each other

tasks.explanation: Alternating traffic fails when flaggers cannot see or hear each other, so positions and a tested release procedure come before the first vehicle is stopped. Relief without handover is a known gap, so the rotation is agreed in advance.

tasks.prompt: Order the advance warning setup for a lane closure that requires a signed detour.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a sewer collapse repair will close one direction of an arterial for three days and traffic will detour on parallel streets.

cards.label: Record the setup check, notifications, and the drive through verification in the project file
Place advance warning signs on the arterial advising of the closure dates and the detour ahead
Close the lane with tapers and barriers only after the detour signing is complete and checked by driving it
Confirm the detour route can carry the arterial traffic, including buses and trucks, with the traffic group
Notify emergency services, transit, and affected businesses of the closure and detour
Place detour signs along the full route before the closure signs go up at the work site

tasks.explanation: A detour signed after the closure traps drivers at the barrier, so the route is signed and driven first. Capacity and notifications protect the surrounding streets, and only a verified detour earns the closure.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a sanitary sewer overflow reaching a roadside ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a blocked collector has overflowed from a manhole and sewage is flowing along a ditch toward a culvert, in a western Canadian municipality.

cards.label: Post warning signs and keep the public and pets away from the affected ditch and any ponded sewage
Notify the supervisor with the location, estimated start, and whether sewage is reaching the ditch, and attend with spill equipment and traffic control
Recover pooled sewage and contaminated material, then clean and disinfect hard surfaces as directed
Contain the flow in the ditch with berms or sandbags ahead of the culvert and arrange a vacuum truck to recover pooled sewage
Record volumes, times, containment, and cleanup for the spill report under provincial requirements and the federal effluent regulations in general terms
Stop or reduce the source by clearing the blockage or arranging bypass pumping, in coordination with operations

tasks.explanation: Notification starts the formal response while the crew moves. Source control limits the volume, containment ahead of the culvert protects the watercourse beyond it, public warning and recovery follow, and the record supports the required reporting.

tasks.prompt: Order the cleanup sequence after an overflow on a grassed and paved area is contained.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow at a lift station site has stopped, sewage ponded on gravel and grass, and no sewage reached a watercourse.

cards.label: Confirm the source is stopped and the station is operating normally before cleanup begins
Wash down hard surfaces toward a recovery point and vacuum the wash water rather than letting it reach a storm drain
Record the cleanup, volumes recovered, and disposal, and attach photos to the spill file
Recover all ponded sewage with the vacuum truck, starting from the lowest pooling point
Apply disinfection to hard surfaces as directed and post the area until it is dry and cleared by the supervisor
Remove contaminated gravel, debris, and any solids from the grassed area by raking and collection

tasks.explanation: Cleanup before the source is proven stopped wastes the effort, so control is confirmed first. Recovery precedes washing, wash water is captured rather than spread, and photos plus records prove the site was returned to a safe condition.

tasks.prompt: Order the documentation and follow up after a sewer overflow event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the overflow is cleaned up, and the operator must complete the event file and the follow up actions in the days after.

cards.label: Brief the crew and supervisor on what the event showed about the section or station involved
Confirm the required notifications were made under provincial wastewater requirements and note the times and names
Attach the response log, photos, containment and cleanup records, and any sampling results to the event file
File the event in the system performance records so it counts in the monthly review and trend reports
Complete the spill report with start and stop times, estimated volume, cause, and the receiving environment affected
Raise a follow up investigation into the cause, such as CCTV or cleaning, with a target date

tasks.explanation: The report is built from the response records while they are complete, notifications are verified rather than assumed, and the cause follow up is raised with a date. Filing the event into performance records is what turns one spill into prevention.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a residential sewer backup call where sewage is in a basement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a homeowner reports sewage in the basement on a street where the municipal main has a history of root blockages.

cards.label: If the main is blocked, set up traffic control and jet from the downstream manhole to clear it, capturing debris at the manhole
Record the caller details, address, and when the backup started, and advise the caller to stop using water and avoid the affected area
Record the findings, the action taken, and the advice given in the service call record the same day
If the main is flowing freely, advise the homeowner the problem is likely in the private service and explain the next steps
Check the downstream and upstream manholes for the property to see whether the municipal main is surcharged or flowing
Confirm flow is restored and check whether neighbouring properties are affected

tasks.explanation: Advice to stop water use limits damage while the cause is located. Manhole checks separate a municipal blockage from a private service problem before any cleaning, and the record of findings and advice protects both the homeowner and the municipality.

tasks.prompt: Order the clearing of a mainline blockage where the upstream manhole is surcharged.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a 300 mm main is blocked, the upstream manhole is surcharged near the rim, and homes upstream are at risk of backup.

cards.label: Jet from the downstream manhole toward the blockage in controlled passes, watching the upstream level
Record the cause if found, the debris removed, and flag the section for CCTV follow up
Set up traffic control at both manholes and warn the supervisor that services are at risk from the surcharge
Continue cleaning until the upstream level returns to normal and flow passes freely
Open the downstream manhole first and confirm it is flowing, so released sewage has somewhere to go
As the blockage releases, control the surge by pausing jetting and vacuuming at the downstream manhole

tasks.explanation: The downstream path is confirmed before the blockage is touched, because releasing a surcharge into a second blockage doubles the problem. Controlled passes and surge management protect upstream homes, and normal levels plus a CCTV flag close the job.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a suspected force main leak reported as sewage surfacing in a ditch.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: public report of sewage and odour in a roadside ditch along the force main route from a duplex lift station.

cards.label: Excavate or expose the main only under an excavation plan with locates, and confirm the leak location and cause
Confirm the surfacing liquid is sewage and identify the nearest force main fittings, valves, and low points from the drawings
Arrange repair, cleanup and disinfection of the affected area, sampling as directed, and complete the spill documentation
Notify the supervisor, record the report details, and attend with spill response equipment and traffic control
Contain the surfacing sewage with berms or a vacuum truck to protect any watercourse and prevent spread
Reduce or stop pumping from the lift station in coordination with operations to limit the leak while keeping the wet well from overflowing

tasks.explanation: Notification and containment thinking start immediately. Drawings locate the likely source, pumping is balanced against wet well overflow risk, containment protects the environment before excavation, and repair plus documented cleanup closes the event.

tasks.prompt: Order the overflow prevention response at a lift station during a power failure without a standby generator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a small station has lost utility power, has no generator, and the wet well is rising during the outage.

cards.label: Notify the supervisor of the overflow risk time so portable equipment can be dispatched early
If an overflow occurs, contain it at the site, post the area, and record the start time and estimated volume
Confirm the outage extent with the utility and estimate the time the wet well can store inflow before overflowing
When power returns, confirm normal automatic operation, remove temporary equipment, and complete the event record
Connect a portable generator or engine driven bypass pump and confirm it holds the level below the alarm point
Monitor the wet well level continuously and arrange tanker hauling if pumping cannot keep up

tasks.explanation: Storage time is calculated first because it decides how fast help must move. Portable pumping is proven against the level, hauling backs it up, and any overflow is contained and recorded rather than discovered later.

tasks.prompt: Order spill containment where an overflow is approaching a creek.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: sewage from a surcharged manhole is flowing overland toward a small creek in a coulee, about 60 m away.

cards.label: Record the containment, whether sewage reached the creek, volumes, and sampling for the spill report
Work on the source in parallel, clearing the blockage or bypass pumping to stop the flow
Vacuum pooled sewage behind the berm and keep recovering until the flow stops
Notify the supervisor at once that a watercourse is threatened and attend with berms, sandbags, and the vacuum truck
Check the creek above and below the entry point and take samples as directed by the supervisor
Build the containment berm across the flow path at the narrowest point before the creek bank

tasks.explanation: A threatened watercourse raises the response level immediately, so notification and berm placement lead. Source control and recovery run together, creek checks and sampling establish whether sewage arrived, and the report records the outcome honestly.

tasks.prompt: Order the public protection steps for an overflow area in a park and pathway system.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow has ponded sewage across a paved pathway in a river valley park, and the area is popular with walkers and dogs.

cards.label: Recover the ponded sewage and wash the pathway with the wash water captured by vacuum, not hosed to the river
Close the affected pathway section with barriers at both ends before starting cleanup work in the area
Keep the closure in place until the supervisor confirms the area is cleaned and safe to reopen
Notify the supervisor and the parks group so public inquiries get one consistent message
Record the closure times, cleanup, and reopening in the spill file
Post clear warning signs at the closures and at park entrances advising people to keep out and keep dogs away

tasks.explanation: Public exclusion comes before cleanup because exposure is the harm being prevented. Signs at entrances reach people before they arrive at the barriers, wash water is captured, and reopening waits for a confirmed clean, not a schedule.

tasks.prompt: Order the sampling and reporting support after a spill that reached a storm pond.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a contained overflow reached the edge of a storm pond, and the supervisor directs sampling and reporting support from the collection operator.

cards.label: Record the spill times, estimated volume, and the point where sewage reached the pond while details are fresh
Keep samples cooled and deliver them to the laboratory or courier within the holding time, with the chain of custody form
File the results and field record in the spill file and confirm the supervisor has them for the required reporting
Collect samples at the locations and times the supervisor directs, using clean bottles and gloves for each sample
Note weather, pond conditions, and any visible effects in the field record attached to the results
Label each sample with location, date, time, and collector name at the moment of collection

tasks.explanation: Sampling only supports reporting if identity, cooling, and custody are right from the moment of collection. Field conditions are recorded with the samples, and the file is complete when the supervisor holds results that can be relied on.

tasks.prompt: Order a timed drawdown test to measure the pumping rate of a lift station pump.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex station, the operator will time one pump drawing down the wet well between two known levels with inflow temporarily held or measured.

cards.label: Calculate the pumping rate from the volume drawn down and the time, and compare it with the pump rated rate
Raise the level above the start point, then run the test pump alone and start timing at the upper level mark
Isolate inflow if the procedure allows, or note the inflow rate so it can be allowed for in the result
Record the result in the station log and raise a work order if the rate is well below the expected value
Record the wet well dimensions or the volume between the test levels from the station record
Stop timing at the lower level mark and record the elapsed time and the levels used

tasks.explanation: The test is only a measurement if the volume and the inflow are known first. Timing between fixed marks gives the rate, comparison with the rated value gives the judgement, and a shortfall becomes a work order, not a note.

tasks.prompt: Order the return to service of a lift station after a vacuum truck has cleaned the wet well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: contract vacuum truck has cleaned the wet well of a duplex station held on bypass pumping during the cleaning.

cards.label: Remove the bypass suction from the wet well in coordination with the vacuum crew and restore normal influent flow
Confirm cleaning is complete and all vacuum hoses, tools, and workers are clear of the wet well
Record the cleaning, any defects found, and the return to service in the station log and work order
Run each pump manually to confirm free operation and correct discharge before using automatic control
Inspect floats, pump intakes, and the wet well floor from the surface and confirm no damage or leftover debris
Return the station to automatic and watch one complete fill and drawdown cycle

tasks.explanation: People and equipment clear, and a surface inspection, come before flow is restored. Manual runs and one watched automatic cycle prove the station before it is left unattended, and the work is documented.

tasks.prompt: Order the wet well grease and ragging inspection and surface cleaning routine.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly surface routine at a duplex station, no entry, using a washdown hose and a rake from the top slab.

cards.label: Inspect the surface for grease mats, float fouling, and debris around the pump intakes from above
Close and secure the cover and record the condition found and the cleaning done in the station log
Review recent run hours and alarms for signs of ragging or grease buildup before opening the wet well cover
Run the pumps to draw the level down and confirm floats move freely through a full cycle
Open the cover, ventilate the headspace, and test the atmosphere at the opening before leaning over the well
Wash down the walls and floats with the station hose and break up surface grease so pumps can draw it down in small amounts

tasks.explanation: History first, then safe opening with ventilation and testing before any surface work. Washing and float checks follow, a proven cycle confirms the result, and the log records the condition for trending.

tasks.prompt: Order the manual verification of wet well level against the monitoring system reading during a round.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the operator suspects the level transmitter may be drifting at a station fitted with both floats and a level transmitter.

cards.label: If the difference exceeds the site tolerance, tag the reading as suspect, rely on float control, and raise a calibration work order
Measure the actual level from the fixed reference point on the top slab with a tape or staff gauge
Record both readings, the difference, and the action taken in the station log
Record the monitoring system level reading and the time before going to the wet well
Raise and lower the level through one pump cycle and confirm the system reading tracks the measured change
Compare the measured level with the system value and note the difference

tasks.explanation: The comparison needs a recorded system value and an independent manual measurement at a known reference. Tracking through a cycle separates a fixed offset from a dead signal, and tagging plus a work order protects operations until calibration.

tasks.prompt: Order the response checks when a round finds one pump with far more run hours than its twin.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: duplex alternating station, the run hour meters show the duty pump has run about three times the hours of the standby this month.

cards.label: Check the control panel alternator setting and confirm it is in automatic alternation, not locked on one pump
Force an alternation and observe the next automatic cycle on the previously idle pump
Record both run hour totals and start counts and compare them with the previous round readings
Record findings in the log and raise a work order for any control or check valve defect found
Run the low hour pump manually and confirm it pumps, draws normal current, and its discharge valve is open
Check the high hour pump discharge check valve for leakage that could be recycling flow back to the well

tasks.explanation: Data first, then the alternator setting, then proving the idle pump actually works. A leaking check valve on the busy pump is checked because it inflates run hours, and a forced alternation proves the fix before leaving.

tasks.prompt: Order the bar screen and influent channel check at a lift station with a manual screen.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: weekly check of the influent screen basket ahead of the wet well at a small station, no entry required.

cards.label: Record the volume of screenings, condition of the basket, and disposal in the station log
Lift the screen basket clear and empty screenings into the lined container for disposal
Wash the basket and channel, inspect for damage, and check the channel for grit and grease buildup
Check flows and wet well behaviour for signs of a blinded screen, such as low inflow with upstream surcharge
Replace the basket fully seated and confirm inflow passes freely into the wet well
Ventilate and test the atmosphere at the screen chamber opening before opening the cover fully

tasks.explanation: Symptoms are checked first, then the chamber is opened safely. Cleaning, inspection, and correct reseating follow in that order, and free inflow plus a log entry close the task.

tasks.prompt: Order a planned manual changeover from the duty pump to the standby pump at a duplex lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: planned changeover for equal wear, both pumps healthy, station in automatic alternation.

cards.label: Return the proven standby pump to automatic as the new duty pump and set the original pump as standby
Record current wet well level, run hours, and starts for both pumps before making any change
Observe one full automatic cycle on the new duty pump and confirm start and stop levels are correct
Place the standby pump in hand and run it to confirm normal flow, current, and discharge before relying on it
Record the changeover, the reason, and the new duty assignment in the station log
Place the duty pump control in the off position and confirm it stops and the level begins to rise slowly

tasks.explanation: Baseline readings come first. The old duty is stopped, the standby is proven in hand before it is trusted in automatic, one full cycle is observed, and the change is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the return of a repaired pump to automatic service after maintenance at a lift station.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: the pump was isolated and locked out for a seal replacement by the maintenance crew, and the work is signed complete.

cards.label: Confirm the maintenance work is complete, all workers are clear, and the work permit or job record is signed off
Run the pump in hand and confirm flow, current, rotation, and no leaks or abnormal noise
Record the return to service, test readings, and the new duty or standby assignment in the station log
Remove lockout devices by the persons who applied them, following the lockout procedure
Place the pump in automatic and observe it start and stop correctly on its floats through one cycle
Confirm the pump is seated, cables are secured clear of the floats, and discharge valves are in the normal position

tasks.explanation: Signed off work and controlled lock removal come before power. Seating, cables, and valves are checked before the hand run, automatic float operation is observed, and the return is logged.

tasks.prompt: Order the sequence for placing a newly replaced submersible pump into service in an existing wet well.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: replacement pump lowered onto the guide rails in a duplex station, the other pump has carried the station during the change.

cards.label: Cycle the pump on its floats in automatic and confirm the check valve closes without slam and the level controls respond
Connect power and control cables, restore the breaker, and remove lockout devices under the lockout procedure
Lower the pump on the guide rails and confirm it seats fully on the discharge elbow with the lifting chain secured at the top
Update the asset record and station log with the new pump serial number, date, and test results
Confirm the replacement pump matches the duty, rotation, voltage, and discharge connection of the original
Run the pump manually and confirm correct rotation by flow, normal current draw, and no abnormal vibration

tasks.explanation: Matching and correct seating come before power is restored. Manual running proves rotation and current before float control is trusted, and the asset record is updated so the next operator knows what is installed.

tasks.prompt: Order the inspection of an air release valve chamber on a sewage force main.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: scheduled inspection of a combination air valve at the high point of a force main, chamber inspection from the surface with the cover open, no entry planned.

cards.label: Test the atmosphere at the opening and inspect the valve body, isolating valve position, and chamber for leakage or corrosion from the surface
Review the force main operating pressure and confirm which pumps are running before opening the chamber
Close and secure the cover, record the valve condition and pressure, and raise work orders for any defects
Confirm the isolating valve is fully open so the air valve can operate, and note any sewage weeping from the valve outlet
Set up traffic control or barriers as needed and open the chamber cover with ventilation at the opening
If the valve is fouled, isolate it by closing the isolating valve and arrange cleaning or replacement under a separate work plan

tasks.explanation: Pressure and pump status set the risk picture before the chamber is opened. Safe opening and testing precede inspection, the isolating valve position is critical because a closed valve disables air release, and findings are recorded with follow up work raised.

tasks.prompt: Order the completion of a sewer cleaning work order record in a CMOM style program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: end of shift, the crew cleaned four sections and the records must support the capacity, management, operations, and maintenance program reporting.

cards.label: Note any defects seen during cleaning, such as roots regrowing or grease returning, against the section record
Close the work order with crew time, equipment, and water use recorded
Confirm the sections cleaned match the asset numbers and lengths on the route plan
Flag sections needing CCTV or a shorter cleaning interval for the program planner
Record the method used, passes made, and the debris type and volume removed for each section
Enter the records into the work order system the same day and attach any photos taken

tasks.explanation: Records written days later lose the debris and defect detail that drives the program. Same day entry tied to asset numbers, with defects and follow up flags, is what makes cleaning history useful for planning.

tasks.prompt: Order the incident file completion for a basement backup claim involving a municipal main blockage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a homeowner has filed a claim after a backup, the main was found blocked with roots, and the file must be complete for the insurer and the supervisor.

cards.label: Have the supervisor review the file for completeness before it goes to the claims contact
Attach the manhole check findings and the cleaning record showing the blockage location and cause
File the incident and flag the section for the root control program so the cause is treated, not only documented
Gather the service call record, crew notes, and the times the call was received and attended
Record the advice and information given to the homeowner and any follow up visits made
Add the cleaning and CCTV history for the section for the years before the event

tasks.explanation: A claim file is judged on contemporaneous records, so call, findings, and cleaning evidence are gathered first. History shows what was known before the event, review precedes release, and the section enters the prevention program.

tasks.prompt: Order the monthly review of collection system performance records.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly review meeting covering blockages, overflows, cleaning production, CCTV completion, and lift station alarms.

cards.label: Compare each measure with the previous months and flag repeat locations and rising trends
Record the review decisions and actions in the program file
Pull the month records for blockages, overflows, cleaning lengths, CCTV lengths, and alarm counts before the meeting
Carry unfinished actions forward to the next month agenda so they are tracked to completion
Match repeat blockage sections against their cleaning intervals and CCTV findings
Agree actions for the worst locations, with owners and dates, such as shorter intervals or rehabilitation candidates

tasks.explanation: The review works from pulled data, not impressions. Trends and repeat locations drive the discussion, actions get owners and dates, and carrying actions forward is what separates a program from a meeting.

tasks.prompt: Order the lift station log review used to trend pump performance over a season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: quarterly desk review of daily logs from six lift stations to find pumps losing capacity or controls drifting before they fail.

cards.label: Record the review findings and the work raised in the station history files
Flag pumps with rising run hours for the same flows, which suggests wear or a recycling check valve
Flag stations with rising start counts, which suggests float or level control problems
Collect the run hours, start counts, and drawdown results for each station for the quarter
Raise inspection work orders for the flagged items ranked by overflow risk
Compare each pump with its twin and with its own results from the previous quarter

tasks.explanation: Trending works by comparison: twin against twin and quarter against quarter. Run hours and starts each point to different fault families, work is ranked by risk, and the history file keeps the evidence for the next review.

tasks.prompt: Order the filing sequence for an overflow report under general provincial and federal requirements.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: an overflow reached a watercourse, verbal notification was already given during the event, and the written report must now be completed.

cards.label: Describe the corrective actions taken and planned to prevent a recurrence at the location
Confirm the verbal notification record, including who was notified, the time, and the information given
Have the supervisor review and submit the report within the time the provincial requirements set
Attach sampling results, photos, containment and cleanup records, and the response log
File the submitted report and reference it in the system performance records and the location history
Complete the written report with location, cause, start and stop times, estimated volume, and the receiving water

tasks.explanation: The written report builds on the verbal record, so that record is confirmed first. Evidence and corrective actions complete the account, review and timely submission meet the requirement, and filing links the event to the location history.

tasks.prompt: Order the handover of flow monitoring data at the end of a wet weather study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a three month flow and rainfall study in two sewersheds is ending and the data must reach the analyst complete and usable.

cards.label: Download the final data from every monitor and confirm no gaps beyond the known battery or fouling outages
Write a short data note listing gaps, suspect periods, and any sewer work that affected flows during the study
Record the study closure and file the package reference in the sewershed record
Check the rainfall record covers the same period and note any missing rain gauge days
Transfer the data package to the analyst and confirm receipt and readability
Attach the site records, installation photos, and the calibration and maintenance visit notes

tasks.explanation: Data without its site history invites wrong conclusions, so completeness, rainfall coverage, and known problems are documented before transfer. Confirmed receipt closes the study, and the sewershed file points to the package for future work.

tasks.prompt: Order the record completion for a grease interceptor inspection at a food service business.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: awareness level task, the operator assisted at an inspection under the fats, oils, and grease program and must complete the record.

cards.label: Leave the business a copy of the inspection result and explain the follow up date
Note the cleaning record shown by the business and the date of the last pump out
Record the measured grease and solids depth as a share of the interceptor capacity
Enter the inspection into the program records and flag overdue corrections for the next visit list
Record the business name, address, interceptor size, and the date and time of the inspection
Record any deficiencies found and the correction time given, in the program standard wording

tasks.explanation: The record must let the next inspector see size, condition, and history at a glance. Measured depth against capacity is the core finding, deficiencies carry a correction time, and the program list drives the follow up.

tasks.prompt: Order the filing of a confined space entry permit after the entry is closed out.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a wet well entry was completed without incident, one gas reading rose mid entry and was managed, and the permit package must be filed.

cards.label: Attach the rescue readiness check and the attendant log to the permit
Confirm the permit is signed closed with entry and exit times and all entrants accounted for
Bring the mid entry gas rise to the supervisor attention for review of the space hazard assessment
Note any procedure or equipment improvements the crew identified during the debrief
Check the atmosphere test record is complete, including the mid entry rise and the action taken
File the permit package where the program requires and record its reference in the station log

tasks.explanation: A permit is a safety record, not just permission, so completeness includes the abnormal reading and how it was handled. Filing links it to the station, and the gas rise feeds back into the hazard assessment for the next entry.

tasks.prompt: Order the asset record update after a lift station pump replacement.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a replacement pump was installed and tested yesterday, and the asset and maintenance records must be made current.

cards.label: Enter the start up test results, including drawdown rate and current draw, as the new baseline
Confirm the station log, asset system, and maintenance system all show the same pump details
Record the new pump make, model, serial number, and installation date from the delivery and test sheets
Set the first preventive maintenance date for the new pump in the maintenance system
Record the removed pump details and its destination, such as repair, spare, or disposal
Update the spare parts list if the new pump uses different seals, cables, or fittings

tasks.explanation: The update starts from source documents, not memory. Baseline test results give future trending its starting point, spares and maintenance dates follow the new equipment, and cross checking the three records prevents the classic mismatch.

tasks.prompt: Order the completion of daily collection records at the end of a shift.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a two person crew finished cleaning, inspections, and one service call, and the foreperson checks records before the crew leaves.

cards.label: Have the foreperson review the entries for completeness and correct asset numbers
Enter the service call findings and the advice given to the resident
Submit the daily records and file the paper field notes as the program requires
Complete each work order with asset numbers, work done, and time on each job while the crew is still together
Pass any unfinished work to the next shift in writing with its status and location
Record equipment defects and low consumables so the next shift is not surprised

tasks.explanation: Records are completed together at shift end because details fade overnight and the crew disperses. Unfinished work is handed over in writing, defects are surfaced for the next shift, and review catches wrong asset numbers before they enter the system.

tasks.prompt: Order the first response to a frozen service call in mid winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a homeowner reports no drainage and a suspected frozen service during a cold snap at minus 28 degrees C in a prairie town.

cards.label: Check recent records for frost depth, past freezing at the address, and whether the main on the street is known to be shallow
Advise the homeowner on the thawing options and responsibilities under the municipal practice, and arrange follow up if the main is involved
Record the address, when drainage stopped, and whether neighbouring homes are affected, and advise the caller to stop adding water
Record the findings, advice, and follow up in the service call record for the winter file
Check the nearest manholes for normal flow in the main to separate a main problem from a service problem
Inspect the cleanout or access point if available for ice at the service, without opening anything under pressure

tasks.explanation: Neighbours and main flow separate a frozen service from a frozen main before anyone thaws the wrong pipe. Records of past freezing guide the response, advice is given under the local practice, and the winter file builds the pattern for prevention.

tasks.prompt: Order a frozen service thawing routine using warm water circulation equipment.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a qualified crew will thaw a frozen residential service from the cleanout using a warm water thawing unit, under municipal practice.

cards.label: Record the thaw location, time taken, and any shallow or damaged section found, and advise the owner on preventing a refreeze
Insert the thawing hose into the service through the cleanout and start warm water circulation at the set temperature
Advance the hose slowly as ice melts, watching return water for the first flow of drainage
Confirm the service is frozen and not blocked, from the call history, manhole checks, and cleanout inspection
Once flow is restored, run water until drainage runs freely and check the main is receiving the flow normally
Set up the thawing unit, confirm hoses and fittings are rated for the work, and protect the work area from water damage

tasks.explanation: Thawing the wrong problem wastes the visit, so freezing is confirmed first. Controlled warm water and a slow advance melt the plug safely, restored flow is proven at the main, and depth notes help prevent the next freeze.

tasks.prompt: Order spring melt readiness checks at a lift station before the melt peak.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: late March in a western Canadian town, snowpack is high, and the station will see melt inflow on top of normal flows for several weeks.

cards.label: Check the high level alarm and dialer or monitoring points and confirm the on call roster for the melt period
Review the station flows from the previous melt season and confirm the pump capacity against the expected peak
Stage bypass hose, a portable pump, and fuel at the station or the yard ready for rapid deployment
Clear snow and ice from the station access, vents, and the wet well cover so the station can be reached and opened quickly
Record the readiness checks and any capacity concerns to the supervisor before the melt begins
Test both pumps on a timed drawdown and confirm the standby generator starts and carries the load

tasks.explanation: Melt readiness is proven capacity, not hope: last year flows set the target, pumps and generator are tested against it, access and alarms are cleared, and bypass gear is staged before the water arrives.

tasks.prompt: Order manhole and station checks during a spring melt surcharge event.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: meltwater inflow has raised flows across an older sewershed, two manholes are surcharged, and the downstream station is running both pumps.

cards.label: Confirm the station is holding the level with both pumps and check the time available if one pump fails
Reduce inflow at the worst points where practical, such as sandbagging a ponded cover, as directed by the supervisor
Record peak levels, inflow points found, and actions taken for the melt season review
Check the surcharged manholes from the surface for displaced covers or overflow, without opening a surcharged cover
Monitor levels and flows at set intervals and report the trend to the supervisor
Look for the main inflow points, such as ponded manholes, broken covers, or a creek crossing taking meltwater

tasks.explanation: Station holding capacity is the first fact, because it sets the urgency of everything else. Surcharged covers are never opened, inflow points are hunted while they are active, and interval reporting keeps the response ahead of the melt curve.

tasks.prompt: Order a winter daily round at a lift station during extreme cold.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: daily round at minus 32 degrees C with wind chill, at a heated duplex station on the edge of a northern community.

cards.label: Clear drifting snow from the door, vents, and exhaust so the next visit and the generator are not blocked
Observe one pump cycle and confirm floats are not held by ice or frozen grease
Check for frozen or split pipes, a frozen sump, and ice at the wet well cover and vent
Record temperatures, any freeze damage, and heater status in the log and report heater faults as urgent
Check the building heater is running and the inside temperature is above freezing before starting the pump checks
Check the generator block heater, battery, and fuel for cold weather readiness

tasks.explanation: In extreme cold the building systems fail before the pumps do, so heat and freeze checks lead the round. Floats and vents are checked for ice specifically, generator cold readiness is confirmed, and a heater fault is urgent because the whole station depends on it.

tasks.prompt: Order the freeze protection check for a wet well and its vent and heat trace systems.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: fall check of a shallow wet well station where the vent froze shut two winters ago and caused control problems.

cards.label: Check insulation on the cover, piping, and the valve chamber for gaps, water damage, or missing sections
Inspect the wet well vent for hoarfrost buildup, damage, and a clear air path before deep cold arrives
Record the check results and complete repairs before the first deep cold period
Confirm the low temperature alarm in the station reports to the monitoring point
Test the heat trace cable on exposed piping and confirm its thermostat and breaker are operating
Run the pumps and confirm discharge piping drains or stays heated as designed after each cycle

tasks.explanation: Freeze protection is checked in fall because repairs in January are emergency work. Vent, heat trace, and insulation are the three defences, the low temperature alarm is the warning system, and every repair is finished before deep cold tests them.

tasks.prompt: Order the response to a frozen air release valve on a force main in winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater collection scenario for Class 1 study. Conditions are as stated in the configuration, and all work follows site procedures, provincial wastewater requirements in general terms, and standard collection practice.
tasks.configuration: Scope: discharge pressure has risen and pumping times have lengthened since a cold snap, and the high point air valve chamber is suspected frozen.

cards.label: Inspect the valve and chamber from the surface for ice around the valve body and a frozen vent outlet
Record the event and arrange insulation or heat improvements for the chamber before the next cold snap
Confirm the pressure trend from the station log and rule out a partly closed valve or pump problem first
Confirm the valve vents air on the next pump cycle and pressures return toward normal
Attend the chamber with traffic control and open the cover carefully, watching for ice holding the cover
