Velocity check in both sewers at similar flow, paired with the CCTV coating start point

tasks.prompt: Grease problems in a downtown Winnipeg sewer get worse every winter and ease every summer with the same restaurant load.

Cold sewage in winter hardens grease deposits, so the same load causes worse narrowing

options.label: Seasonal CCTV and sewage temperature log for the same reach over one full year
Restaurant sales records by month
Tree growth records for downtown

clueText.nc-b: Sales records do not measure what hardened inside the pipe.

tasks.prompt: A home in a Calgary suburb reports a backup, and the crew finds solid white fat in the home lateral and in the main at the connection.

tasks.prompt: Crews in a British Columbia coastal town find grease only in the first 20 m below a manhole, and the rest of a long reach is clean.

tasks.prompt: A sewer serving a food processing plant in Manitoba blocks with a pale solid that looks like grease, but it does not melt in hot water the way grease does.

The blockage is root mass bleached pale by sewage

Paired samples, plant lateral discharge and pipe deposit, with matching lab screening results

CCTV of the classroom wing lateral

tasks.prompt: A residential street in a prairie city reports slow drains at three homes, all downstream of one large cottonwood tree.

tasks.prompt: Sewage backs up into a basement during dry weather on a street in Regina with mature trees and old clay pipe.

tasks.prompt: A sewer reach in a British Columbia valley town needs jetting every month, always at the same location, while nearby reaches stay clear for years.

tasks.prompt: A root problem is suspected in a Winnipeg suburb, but CCTV shows the main is clear while one home keeps backing up.

tasks.prompt: Flow in a 250 mm sewer in Alberta is slow, and CCTV shows a white fibrous mass hanging from the top of the pipe at one joint.

tasks.prompt: Two homes at the low end of a court in Saskatoon back up whenever the sewer is jetted from the upstream manhole.

Homes at the high end of the court never back up.
The downstream trunk sewer is flowing at normal depth at the same time.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: The jetting nozzle is spraying water directly into the home laterals
The homes have no backwater valves, so any flow backs them up at all times
A downstream trunk collapse is holding back all flow at all times
Jetting water cannot pass the root restriction fast enough, so it surcharges to the low homes

inference.explanation: Backups only during jetting, a half full root mass at the low end, and rapid recovery when jetting stops all fit a restriction that passes normal flow but not jetting flow. A total downstream holdback would affect normal flow too.

nextClue.prompt: Which trial best confirms the restriction theory before root cutting?

options.label: Jet at reduced flow with a camera at the root mass and watch manhole levels during the trial
Review rainfall records for the jetting days
Install backwater valves in the two homes and jet at full flow

nextClue.explanation: A reduced flow trial with level watching tests whether flow rate through the restriction drives the surcharge, without flooding homes.

clueText.nc-a: At half jetting flow the manhole level stays normal and the camera shows water passing the root mass steadily.
clueText.nc-b: The backups occur in dry weather during jetting, so rainfall is not the driver.
clueText.nc-c: Valves protect homes but do not test what is restricting the main.

tasks.prompt: Roots are heavy in a clay sewer in a mountain town, but one short section of newer plastic pipe in the same run has no roots at all.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian mixed material sewer run. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Clay sections show roots at most joints on CCTV.
The plastic section has tight gasketed joints and shows no root entry.
Tree cover and soil conditions are the same over the whole run.
Flow and cleaning history are the same for both materials.
The plastic section is the same age as the last clay repair beside it.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots enter through the open clay joints, and tight plastic joints deny them entry
The plastic pipe repels roots because of its smooth inner wall alone
Trees avoid the plastic section because it is newer
The camera missed roots in the plastic section because it moved faster there

inference.explanation: Same trees, soil, flow, and cleaning isolate joint type as the difference: open clay joints admit roots, tight joints do not. Smoothness alone does not explain entry at joints specifically.

nextClue.prompt: Which comparison best supports a joint sealing repair choice?

options.label: Jetting pressure records for the run
Joint by joint CCTV defect log comparing root entry at clay joints versus plastic joints
Tree species inventory for the street

nextClue.explanation: A joint by joint log ties root entry to joint condition, which is what a sealing repair must address.

clueText.nc-a: Jetting pressure was the same and does not explain entry at joints only.
clueText.nc-b: The log shows root entry at 14 of 16 clay joints and at none of the plastic joints in the same run.
clueText.nc-c: Tree species are the same over both sections, so an inventory cannot explain the contrast.

tasks.prompt: A sewer under a park in a prairie town blocks each spring and clears each fall with no cleaning done in between.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian park sewer with a seasonal pattern. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Blockages are reported in April and May in three separate years.
CCTV in June shows fresh pale root tips growing into the pipe at several joints.
CCTV the following January shows the same joints with much less root mass.
Rainfall in the blockage months is near normal and nearby streets do not block.
The park irrigation system is off during the blockage months.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Spring rainfall inflow overloads this sewer each year
Seasonal root growth into the pipe peaks in spring and dies back by winter
Park irrigation lines leak into the sewer each spring
Winter freezing blocks the pipe and spring thaw clears it

inference.explanation: Fresh growing tips in June, dieback by January, and normal rainfall with clear neighbouring streets fit a growth cycle. Freezing would block in winter, the opposite of the observed pattern, and irrigation is off.

nextClue.prompt: Which record best confirms the seasonal growth cycle for scheduling treatment?

options.label: Park irrigation schedules
Frost depth records for the park
CCTV from the same joints in spring, summer, and winter in one year, logged with dates

nextClue.explanation: Same joint dated images across seasons directly document growth and dieback for treatment timing.

clueText.nc-a: Irrigation schedules do not explain root tips seen growing at the joints.
clueText.nc-b: Frost records cannot explain blockages that peak in spring and clear by fall.
clueText.nc-c: Dated images show pale new growth in May, a full mass in August, and a thin mass the next January.

tasks.prompt: A manhole in a Calgary neighbourhood grows a root mass inside the manhole itself while the pipes entering it stay mostly clear.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian manhole root mass. Observations are as stated.

evidence.label: Roots hang from the manhole wall joints above the channel.
CCTV of both entering pipes shows only light root hairs at one pipe joint.
A large tree stands within 2 m of the manhole.
Jetting the pipes does not reduce the manhole root mass.
The mass traps rags and paper and slows flow through the channel.

inference.prompt: Which explanation is best supported by all of the observations?

options.label: Roots are washing down from the upstream pipe and collecting in the manhole
The upstream pipe is full of roots that the camera cannot reach
Roots are entering through the manhole wall joints and the mass is growing in the manhole, not mainly in the pipes
Rags from homes are forming the whole mass without any roots

inference.explanation: The mass hangs from the manhole wall joints, pipe jetting does not shrink it, and the pipes show only light hairs. A washed down mass would sit in the channel, not hang from wall joints.

nextClue.prompt: Which inspection best confirms the entry points before sealing work?

options.label: Close visual and camera inspection of each manhole wall joint with root entry points marked on a manhole diagram
A second full CCTV run of the upstream pipe
A rag count from the downstream lift station

nextClue.explanation: Marking entry at the wall joints themselves is the direct evidence a sealing repair needs.

clueText.nc-a: The diagram marks roots entering at four wall joints, matching the hanging mass positions.
clueText.nc-b: A second pipe run repeats a view that already showed only light hairs.
clueText.nc-c: Station rag counts do not locate where roots enter this manhole.
